transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-11 15:00 PST | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Laura (Northbridge), Markus (Northbridge), Priya (Northbridge)

Summary: quick scoping for a POC primarily focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. We want to validate latency SLOs and unit cost across our fraud scoring and KYC pipelines.

00:00 Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira with Redwood, Diego our SE is here too — just to confirm names and roles?
00:08 Laura: Hi Samira, Laura Chen here, Head of Data & ML at Northbridge. Markus is infra and Priya is security.
00:14 Markus: yea, hi
00:16 Diego: great, thanks. quick agenda: success criteria, expected traffic profile (QPS, concurrency), token distributions per request, and the benchmark plan and timelines. we'll also cover security notes briefly.
00:28 Laura: sounds good. high level for us: we need <150ms tail latency p50/p95 for the fraud scoring path, and we care about sustained throughput during business hours. cost matters but reliability and SLO is top priority.
00:42 Samira: noted. can you share current qps and concurrency numbers for those two flows?
00:48 Laura: for fraud, peak QPS during fraud spikes is about 800 to 1.2k qps, sustained at maybe 300 qps. concurrency... we measure concurrent requests as roughly 150 to 250 during spikes. KYC is lower qps but each request is much larger — about 1k to 1.8k input tokens and 150 to 400 output tokens.
01:12 Diego: okay that's helpful. so for fraud scoring we should model short inputs, maybe 40 to 120 input tokens and 20 to 50 output tokens. We need to model both small and medium sequences to see batching effects and KV cache behaviors.
01:27 Priya: on security, we'll need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs retained for 12 months. we also want to ensure token leakage is impossible — can you confirm you support on-prem key management in Private?
01:39 Samira: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and vpc-only endpoints; for the POC we recommend Dedicated in our hosted VPC with a KMS integration — it's quicker — unless you want a private deployment.
01:54 Markus: timeline matters — we need to show results to ops by mid-February. what's your typical POC timeline?
01:58 Diego: typical POC is 4–6 weeks: week 0 onboarding and infra setup, week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 tuning (batching/quantization), week 3 production-like load tests and final evaluation. for your dates that maps to our suggested benchmark window in early January for final validation, though we can shift.
02:20 Laura: ok, baseline metrics we care about: p50/p95 latencies, tokens per second, gpu utilization, and per-token cost. also quality — false positive change for fraud model shouldn't degrade more than 0.5%.
02:32 Diego: we'll capture per-route token breakdown, and can instrument per-token cost; Redwood Console gives per-route latency and token cost, plus rollup dashboards.
02:40 Samira: on traffic modeling, can you confirm distribution across hours? is the 1k qps constant or bursts?
02:46 Laura: bursts — mostly business hours 9–5, with peaks around 11a and 3p. bursts can be 5–8 minutes long. weekend traffic is about 20% of weekdays.
03:00 Diego: for benchmark sim we'll create a load profile csv: minute-level QPS, percent of requests with long tokens (KYC), and concurrent users. target test scenarios: 1) steady 300 QPS for 1 hour, 2) burst scenario 1k QPS for 10 minutes with ramp, 3) large-request test simulating KYC at 200 qps with big token sizes.
03:23 Markus: what concurrency are you modeling per GPU? we need to ensure dedicated pools are sized appropriately.
03:28 Diego: depends on model and VM type; rule of thumb for 8-bit quantized 30B model on A100-ish is about 8-12 qps per GPU for long contexts; but with batching and 2x concurrency you can get higher. we'll run model-specific sizing in the baseline.
03:44 Laura: we plan to test multiple model variants — smaller for fraud scoring and larger for KYC. can Redwood route to model variants automatically if capacity is constrained?
03:53 Samira: yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible quantized variant; we can model an A/B with canary traffic. we'll include fallback policies in the POC config.
04:03 Priya: for benchmarks we need reproducible datasets; we can't use PII, so we'll provide sanitized samples or synthetic generator. what's your preferred format?
04:11 Diego: CSV or ndjson with fields: request_id, input_text, expected_output_tokens. we'll also accept a small sample of real-ish anonymized text to calibrate tokenization.
04:20 Laura: we'll do sanitized samples + a synthetic generator for scale. expect to provide by end of next week.
04:28 Diego: perfect. regarding metrics, we'll export Prometheus and have a dashboard in Redwood Console. also we'll capture token-level cost for each route and an SLO report.
04:39 Markus: can you share the benchmark script now or after the call?
04:43 Diego: I'll share a starting JMeter/locust script and a load profile csv by Monday. it simulates concurrent clients and can reproduce ramp/burst patterns.
04:51 Laura: quality acceptance — for fraud, we need to ensure the model's score distribution doesn't drift; how do you suggest we validate quality during POC?
04:57 Diego: we suggest a set of holdout prompts and golden labels; we'll run evals each benchmark and compute precision/recall changes. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions beyond a threshold, we'll configure for 0.5% tolerance.
05:11 Samira: cost targets, any ballpark? we can model different batch sizes and concurrency to show cost per 1M tokens for both flows.
05:20 Laura: we want to compare hosted vs dedicated pricing — if dedicated saves >35% cost for our expected workload it's compelling.
05:28 Diego: totally — we'll produce a cost model spreadsheet with assumptions: qps, avg tokens per request, average request length, and GPU hourly pricing. we'll model caching effects — prefix caching for repeated requests helps fraud scoring a lot.
05:44 Markus: about network egress and regional constraints — our production is in eu-west-1; can you run Dedicated nodes there?
05:49 Samira: yes, we have dedicated capacity in eu-west-1; for Private we can run on-prem but that's longer lead time.
05:56 Priya: also need SAML SSO for console and RBAC controls so auditors can see logs. can you confirm log retention options?
06:02 Samira: we support SAML, role-based access, and audit logs configurable up to multi-year retention as an add-on.
06:10 Laura: ok next steps and dates?
06:13 Samira: action items recap — I'll send SOW and pricing by Dec 15, Diego sends bench scripts by Dec 14, Priya to share compliance pack by Dec 13, Laura to provide sanitized datasets by Dec 20. benchmark week tentatively Jan 10-17.
06:31 Laura: sounds good, one question — can we run an initial smoke test before the full benchmark to check connectivity and KMS?
06:37 Diego: yes, we'll do a 1–2 day smoke validation during onboarding to validate VPC peering and KMS key setup.
06:45 Samira: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and shared drive links for artifacts.
06:50 Markus: thanks
06:52 Priya: thanks
06:53 Laura: thanks all

End of transcript.
